test_cases.test_name: End-to-End Workflow Template Configuration and Execution
test_cases.objective: Verify that the platform can successfully configure and execute a complete personalized therapy workflow from apheresis through to infusion, enforcing all configured rules and handoffs.
prerequisites: System installation is complete and verified
Test environment with configured user roles is available
Sample workflow template configuration data is prepared
Test patient and manufacturing lot data is loaded

test_steps.action: Log into the system with administrator credentials and navigate to the workflow template configuration module.
test_steps.expected_result: System authenticates user and displays the workflow template configuration interface successfully.

test_steps.action: Configure a new end-to-end workflow template including apheresis, manufacturing slot allocation, QC release, and infusion steps with defined constraints.
test_steps.expected_result: System saves the workflow template configuration without errors and displays a confirmation message.

test_steps.action: Initiate the configured workflow for a test patient and proceed through each step, performing dual-scanning verification at handoff points.
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow progresses through all stages correctly, enforcing chain-of-identity and chain-of-custody requirements at each handoff.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for each handoff

test_steps.action: Verify that the system generates a complete audit trail and requires e-signatures for critical actions as configured.
test_steps.expected_result: Complete audit trail is generated for all workflow steps and e-signatures are required and captured for critical actions.

acceptance_criteria: Workflow template configuration is saved and retrievable without data loss
All configured workflow steps execute in the correct sequence
Dual-scanning verification is enforced at all handoff points
Complete audit trail is generated for the entire workflow execution
E-signatures are required and captured for all critical actions as per 21 CFR Part 11
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
GDP guidelines for chain-of-custody documentation
GAMP 5 for configured systems validation
data_integrity_requirements: All workflow steps must generate immutable audit trail entries
Chain-of-identity must be maintained throughout the workflow
Electronic signatures must be cryptographically secured
All configuration changes must be version-controlled
urs_requirements: URS-028-001: Configure end-to-end workflow templates
URS-028-002: Enforce chain-of-identity and chain-of-custody
URS-028-009: 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures for critical actions
related_tests: OQ-002: Exception Handling Workflow Testing
OQ-003: Risk Scoring Rules Verification

test_cases.test_name: Exception Handling Workflow for Temperature Excursions

test_steps.expected_result: System detects the temperature excursion and automatically triggers the exception handling workflow.

test_steps.action: Verify that the system generates appropriate notifications to designated personnel and routes the shipment through the exception workflow.
test_steps.expected_result: Notifications are sent to correct personnel and the shipment is placed in quarantine or exception status as configured.

test_steps.action: Follow the exception workflow steps including investigation, impact assessment, and required approvals for disposition decision.
test_steps.expected_result: System guides users through all exception workflow steps and captures all required approvals and investigation details.

acceptance_criteria: Temperature excursions are automatically detected when thresholds are exceeded

Appropriate personnel receive notifications as configured
All exception handling steps require proper documentation and approvals

21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and approvals
ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management principles
data_integrity_requirements: All temperature readings must be recorded with timestamp and device identity
Exception workflow actions must be captured in immutable audit trails

URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events
URS-028-010: Compliance with GDP for logistics and cold-chain records

test_cases.test_name: Dual-Scanning Verification Failure Handling and Recovery
test_cases.objective: Verify the system correctly handles and recovers from dual-scanning verification failures during chain-of-identity/custody events, ensuring data integrity and appropriate workflow escalation.
prerequisites: System configured with dual-scanning verification rules
Test patient journey created with apheresis and manufacturing steps
Two authorized users with barcode scanners available
Exception handling workflows configured for scanning failures

test_steps.action: Initiate a material handoff step in an active patient workflow requiring dual-scanning verification
test_steps.expected_result: System prompts for first user scan and displays scanning interface

test_steps.action: Perform first successful scan with valid credentials and material barcode
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts first scan and prompts for second user verification

test_steps.action: Attempt second scan with mismatched material barcode or invalid user credentials
test_steps.expected_result: System rejects the scan and displays appropriate error message

test_steps.action: Verify system prevents workflow progression and triggers exception handling
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow pauses at handoff step and exception workflow is initiated

test_steps.action: Complete corrective action through exception workflow and retry dual-scanning
test_steps.expected_result: System allows retry and successfully completes dual-scanning verification

acceptance_criteria: System must reject mismatched or invalid second scans with clear error messaging
Workflow progression must be blocked until successful dual-scanning completion
All scanning attempts and failures must be recorded in audit trail
Exception handling workflow must be triggered automatically upon verification failure
System must maintain data integrity throughout failure and recovery process
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic records integrity and access controls
GDP guidelines for material handling and verification procedures
Chain-of-identity/chain-of-custody regulatory requirements
data_integrity_requirements: All scan attempts (successful and failed) must be timestamped and user-attributed
Audit trail must capture the complete sequence of verification events
No partial or incomplete verification states should be allowed to persist
Exception workflow actions must be fully documented and traceable

URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events
related_tests: OQ-003: Chain-of-Identity and Chain-of-Custody Verification with Dual-Scanning
OQ-013: Audit Trail Completeness and Immutability Verification

test_cases.test_name: Custom Algorithm Module Version Control and Rollback Capability
test_cases.objective: Verify the system properly manages custom algorithm module versions, including deployment, activation, and rollback capabilities while maintaining system stability.
prerequisites: Platform with container orchestration capabilities installed
Multiple versions of a custom algorithm module available in repository
System administrator access with deployment permissions
Test patient data sets for algorithm validation

test_steps.action: Deploy version 1.2 of a custom patient matching algorithm module to the staging environment
test_steps.expected_result: Module deploys successfully and appears in module management interface

test_steps.action: Activate version 1.2 and verify it processes test patient data correctly
test_steps.expected_result: Algorithm processes data and produces valid matching results with explainability artifacts

test_steps.action: Deploy and activate version 1.3 of the same algorithm module
test_steps.expected_result: New version deploys alongside version 1.2 without disrupting active workflows

test_steps.action: Execute patient matching using version 1.3 and compare results with version 1.2
test_steps.expected_result: Both versions remain operational and produce version-specific results

test_steps.action: Initiate rollback procedure to revert to version 1.2 as active production version
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully deactivates version 1.3 and reactivates version 1.2

test_steps.action: Verify all version changes are recorded in deployment audit trail
test_steps.expected_result: Complete deployment history with timestamps and user attribution is maintained

acceptance_criteria: System must support simultaneous deployment of multiple algorithm versions
Version activation and deactivation must not disrupt active patient workflows
Rollback procedures must complete within defined maintenance windows
All version changes must be fully documented in audit trails
Algorithm explainability artifacts must include version identification
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - System configuration management and change control
GAMP 5 guidelines for configurable systems and custom software
FDA guidance on software version control in medical devices
data_integrity_requirements: Algorithm version must be recorded with all patient matching decisions
Deployment and activation events must be immutably logged
Version-specific configurations must be preserved during rollback operations
Explainability artifacts must clearly identify algorithm version used
urs_requirements: URS-028-015: Custom algorithm modules shall be containerized and versioned
URS-028-016: Provide explainability artifacts for algorithm decisions
URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events
